criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear description of mission goals, users (marine/conservation scientists) and rationale (GBR bleaching). References provided. Lacks explicit mission requirements (e.g., resolution, revisit, coverage) so not fully complete.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt chart and task descriptions show a feasible plan. Lacks contingency provisions and a dedicated list of planned information sources. Plan is basic but sufficient to believe project can be completed.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: No technical results or calculations presented. Only intention stated, with a major orbital mechanics error (GEO at 600 km). Some background work and tutorials completed, but no preliminary design results.

evidence.quote: My current choice is a geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Well-structured with clear headings and readable prose. Gantt chart labelled. No reference list (only footnotes) and minor inconsistency between text and Gantt for editing weeks. Overall presentation is adequate but not fully professional.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs harbour some of the most diverse species of life on the planet

technical_issues.issue: Geostationary orbit at 600 km is incorrect; GEO altitude is ~35,786 km. 600 km is LEO.
Inconsistency: text says weeks 7-8 for editing, Gantt shows weeks 9-10.
No reference list; only footnotes, which may not satisfy proper citation format.
Abbreviation 'AOEs' unclear; likely meant argument of perigee but non-standard.

overall: Compelling mission concept with good rationale and references, but project plan lacks detail and contingency. Preliminary technical work is minimal and contains a significant orbital error. Presentation is adequate but missing a reference list.

feedback.summary: Your report presents a compelling coral-bleaching relay mission with clear users and rationale, and a readable structure. To strengthen it, add explicit mission requirements, a more detailed plan with contingencies and information sources, and preliminary technical results. Correct the GEO altitude error and include a reference list.
next_steps: Add explicit mission requirements (e.g., spatial resolution, revisit interval, coverage, data latency) and link each to user needs in the Mission Concept & Rationale.

Expand the Project Plan: include a dedicated information-sources list, contingency provisions, and align the text with the Gantt chart (e.g., editing weeks 7–8 vs 9–10); define abbreviations such as AOEs.
Produce preliminary technical results (e.g., orbit trade study or link budget) and correct the orbital altitude: GEO is ~35,786 km, not 600 km; document calculations and interpretation.

criteria.C1: You clearly identify marine/conservation scientists as users and justify the mission with GBR bleaching and references. To reach Accomplished, add explicit mission requirements—resolution, revisit, coverage, latency—and tie each to user needs. This will complete the goals-to-requirements chain.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart and task descriptions show a feasible plan. For Accomplished, add contingency provisions and a dedicated list of planned information sources, and explain why the plan fits the mission narrative. Also resolve the text–Gantt inconsistency for editing weeks and define 'AOEs'.
criteria.C3: You have completed STK tutorials, but no preliminary technical results are presented. To move beyond Deficient, include a small set of results with brief interpretation—e.g., an orbit trade study or coverage estimate. Correct the significant error: GEO altitude is ~35,786 km, not 600 km; 600 km is LEO.
criteria.C4: Your document is well structured with clear headings and readable prose, and the Gantt chart is labelled. For Accomplished, add a proper reference list (not only footnotes), ensure in-text citations match it, and make formatting fully consistent—including aligning the text and Gantt chart on editing weeks.
